questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Solution of an Intermediate System Using the LU Factorization of a 3x3 Matrix
questions.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=1 \\ -2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-2 \\ -{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}+{y}_{3}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =1, \\ {y}_{2} & =-2+2{y}_{1} \\  & =-2+2(1) \\  & =0, \\ {y}_{3} & =2+{y}_{1}-{y}_{2} \\  & =2+(1)-(0) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$y=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}].$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 Linear System Using LU Factorization
questions.problem:
Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $b,$ given by

$$
A={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U},\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

If $⟨{x}_{1},{x}_{2}⟩$ and $⟨{y}_{1},{y}_{2}⟩$ are the solutions to the systems $Ax=b$ and $Ly=b$ respectively, what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {y}_{1}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the two systems in turn.

- First, we solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=3 \\ -2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-3.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=3$ and ${y}_{2}=3.$ Therefore, 

$$
y=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

- Next, we solve $Ux=y.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=y=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=3 \\ 2{x}_{2}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${x}_{2}=\frac{3}{2}$ and ${x}_{1}=-\frac{3}{2}.$ Therefore, 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{3}{2} \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}\cdot {y}_{1}=-\frac{3}{2}\cdot 3=-\frac{9}{2}.$

questions.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 Linear System Using LU Factorization
questions.problem:
Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $b,$ given by

$$
A={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U},\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

If $⟨{x}_{1},{x}_{2}⟩$ and $⟨{y}_{1},{y}_{2}⟩$ are the solutions to the systems $Ax=b$ and $Ly=b$ respectively, what is the value of ${x}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the two systems in turn.

- First, we solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}]=b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=3 \\ 2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=3$ and ${y}_{2}=-2.$ Therefore, 

$$
y=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

- Next, we solve $Ux=y.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -5 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=y=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-5{x}_{2}=3 \\ 2{x}_{2}=-2,\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${x}_{2}=-1$ and ${x}_{1}=-1.$ Therefore, 

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, ${x}_{1}^{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}=(-1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}=5.$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Solution of an Intermediate System Using the LU Factorization of a 2x2 Matrix
questions.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -7 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 22\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that 

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -7 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 22\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=-6 \\ -7{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=22.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is ${y}_{1}=-6$ and ${y}_{2}=-20.$ 

Therefore, $y=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -20\end{aligned}].$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Solution of an Intermediate System Using the LU Factorization of a 3x3 Matrix
questions.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $b,$ given by 

$$
L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 7 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $y$ such that

$$
{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $Ax=b.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $Ux=y,$ we obtain

$$
L{{(Ux)}_{⏟}}_{y}=b\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y.\end{aligned}
$$

We now solve $Ly=b.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 7 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} \\ {y}_{2} \\ {y}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

This gives the system of equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=5 \\ -2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=2 \\ 7{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}+{y}_{3}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =5, \\ {y}_{2} & =2+2{y}_{1} \\  & =2+2(5) \\  & =12, \\ {y}_{3} & =-1-7{y}_{1}-{y}_{2} \\  & =-1-7(5)-(12) \\  & =-48.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
$y=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 12 \\ -48\end{aligned}].$
